related_questions.question: What is the inflation rate currently in the US?
related_questions.snippet: What is the current inflation rate? Over the past 12 months, the overall annual inflation rate in June hit 2.7 percent, the BLS' CPI report showed. Excluding food and energy, “core” prices rose 2.9 percent from a year ago. Inflation is well below where it peaked in the summer of 2022.

related_questions.question: Is US inflation coming down?
related_questions.snippet: The 12-month CPI inflation rate rose from an average of 2.1% over 2017-2019 to 9.0% in June 2022, alarming economists and the public. Then, inflation started declining and in March 2025 it stood at 2.4%, most of the way back to its pre-pandemic level.

related_questions.question: Are prices rising in the US?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, prices are rising in the US, but the rate of increase has slowed. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 2.7% over the past 12 months, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). This is an increase from 2.4% in May. The core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 2.9% over the same period. While still elevated, these figures indicate that inflation is moderating compared to the peak seen in 2022.
